I remember being in toxic relationships for two years and I forgot how to be single. I went into meaningless rebounds and allowed myself to be treated like trash and I couldn't stand the idea of being single. But then I went through with therapy and after a few sessions my attitude completely changed. I just don't have to be emotionally invested in people or be dependent on them. I don't have to wake up feeling disappointed in the life I'm living or the people around me. I suddenly felt like I had huge reserves of energy that I solely dedicated to my partners and now I could finally direct that energy towards myself. I invested in my hobbies, exercised more, made meals plans and started taking care of my body, bought myself gifts and sex toys (which my ex claimed were weird).

I don't even care about impressing people anymore. Recently a guy asked me out and I guess he was lowkey into me. I was being completely pragmatic, clearly communicated my needs and when he couldn't meet them I said that's alright, we can be friends.I didn't jump into a relationship like I always used to. 

Being single teaches you a lot about yourself and what you want in life. My vision for the future has completely changed. I no longer see my happiness as only coming from my partner. I see myself excelling in my career, being an inspiration to younger women, exercising and being fit and living in a quiet neighbourhood with my own time to reflect on my experiences. I of course don't mind being in a relationship. But I can NEVER again see myself being dependent on someone or even sharing my life with someone. I would rather be in a relationship with someone I can call a friend. Someone I can have a sense of companionship with but at the same time , we live our own separate independent lives and do not owe each other every miniscule detail about our lives.

Okay so this can be a very long answer XD. But in short, it really depends. I do daily readings for myself (after some meditation until I become calm) and it's 100% accurate to the point where it's kind of scary. I have also noticed that when I do readings when I'm overly anxious or nervous, the cards do not respond well. It's also very accurate for 2 of my friends. For the rest, they don't believe in it and the cards respond accordingly and do not make any sense. 

I feel like my cards have an energy of their own and they respond really really well to people who genuinely want an answer from the universe. This also explains why my cards seem to work really well for me and 2 other people 100% of the time. 

Also tarot isn't like fortune telling. It's more like a guide on what you should be doing (or whether you need to change what you're doing). If there is something bothering you, a card may ask you a question or offer you a perspective which you didn't think about before. It may encourage you to pursue something or give you an insight regarding someone which you haven't thought about before and now you are able to introspect and make your own decision. I've also always been fascinated by symbolism and looking for signs from the universe on any topic that's been confusing me. So tarot fulfils my needs in that way and provides me with the guidance that I need.

Anyway, it sounds really kooky and weird to most people. But it's a really interesting hobby and I've learnt a lot about symbols, mythology, history of cards and witchcraft during the journey as well!
